paths.title: Feature and Target Design
paths.description: Define prediction time, labels, features, splits, and leakage controls.
concept: A feature is valid only if it is available with the same meaning when the model makes its prediction.
Leakage often enters through future events, post-outcome fields, aggregates, or preprocessing fitted before the split.
workflow: Design a leakage-resistant dataset
Build examples around the real decision timestamp.
The dataset should reproduce what the system would know at inference time.
Define the prediction event and horizon.
Define the target and labeling window.
List features with availability times.
Split data before learned preprocessing.
Use grouped or temporal splits when needed.
Audit features for downstream outcome information.
Document exclusions and assumptions.
question: Detect target leakage
A model predicts hospital readmission at discharge. Which feature is invalid?
Age recorded at admission
Length of stay known at discharge
A follow-up outcome recorded two weeks later
Diagnosis recorded before discharge
The follow-up outcome occurs after prediction time and would not be available in real use.
checklist: Confirm that training examples represent future inference.
Data documentation should make temporal and ownership assumptions visible.
Preprocessing is fitted only on training data.

paths.title: Model Evaluation and Calibration
paths.description: Choose metrics, thresholds, baselines, and uncertainty that match the decision.
concept: Model quality cannot be summarized meaningfully without decision costs, class balance, and the operating threshold.
Accuracy may be misleading for rare events, while ranking metrics do not guarantee calibrated probabilities.
workflow: Evaluate a candidate model
Compare against a simple baseline and intended operating conditions.
Evaluation must use untouched data that represents deployment.
Define the decision and error costs.
Choose a baseline.
Select metrics before tuning.
Keep a final test set untouched.
Report performance by important groups.
Choose thresholds using validation data.
Check calibration and uncertainty.
Document failure cases.
question: Evaluate rare-event detection
Only 1% of cases are positive. Which result can still be useless despite 99% accuracy?
A model predicting every case as negative
A calibrated model with useful recall
A model evaluated by precision and recall
A model compared with a baseline
Always predicting the majority class reaches 99% accuracy while detecting no positive cases.
checklist: Ensure that a headline score does not hide operational failure.
The report should support a threshold and deployment decision, not only rank models.
Calibration is checked when probabilities are used.
The test set was not used for tuning.

paths.title: Deployment and Monitoring
paths.description: Serve models with versioned features, guarded releases, drift detection, and rollback.
concept: A model is one component of a prediction system
Production behavior depends on feature pipelines, schemas, latency, thresholds, downstream actions, and feedback loops.
A correct model artifact can still fail when features are stale, reordered, missing, or interpreted differently.
workflow: Release a model safely
Verify compatibility before allowing the model to influence decisions.
Shadow and limited rollouts reveal integration defects before full exposure.
Version the model and feature schema.
Reproduce offline metrics from the packaged artifact.
Validate online feature parity.
Run in shadow mode when feasible.
Compare latency and predictions with the current model.
Roll out to a bounded cohort.
Monitor outcomes and drift.
Keep a tested rollback path.
question: Identify feature drift
What does feature drift describe?
A change in the distribution of model inputs over time
A new filename for the model
A larger code comment
A guaranteed decline in every metric
Input distributions can shift even before labels arrive; the performance impact must then be investigated.
checklist: Confirm that model behavior remains observable and reversible.
Monitoring should cover the system, inputs, predictions, and delayed outcomes.
Input and prediction distributions are monitored.
Outcome metrics are measured when labels arrive.
Human override paths are defined where needed.
